summary.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.4% YoY to INR 655 crores, with PAT up 55.8% to INR 57 crores and facility guidance raised to 65 additions.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 31.4% YoY to INR 655 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA up 28.8% to INR 186 crores at a stable margin near 28%. PAT rose 55.8% YoY to INR 57 crores, with PAT margin up about 134 bps to 8.5%, despite start-up losses at newer centres. Management added 21 facilities in Q2 (19 Greenfield plus 2 acquired in Delhi NCR) and raised FY27 guidance to 65 facility additions, including 55 surgical centres, with capex raised from INR 400 crores to INR 500 crores. SSSG was 18.8% in Q2 and 17.7% in H1, and the company disclosed its first acquisition in a while (INR 55 crores, two Delhi NCR centres).

financial_highlights.change: +50 bps YoY; gross margin INR 1,014 crores, +28.4%
vs INR 111.2 crores in Q2 FY26

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Largest region at 62% of group revenue; H1 FY27 revenue INR 790 crores, up 24.6% YoY, driven by refractive, retina, cornea, pharmacy and optical.

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: 15% of group revenue; H1 INR 195 crores, up about 30% YoY; 55 facilities including 8 new Greenfield additions in H1.

segments.name: North region
segments.commentary: 9% of group revenue; H1 INR 115 crores, up 60% YoY; 36 facilities, 13 added this year. Delhi NCR network now 15 facilities after 5 Greenfield and 2 acquired centres.

segments.name: East region
segments.commentary: Small contributor; H1 revenue INR 35 crores, up 30% YoY; 14 facilities under new leadership.

segments.name: Africa operations
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 31.1% YoY, about 10.4% of group revenue in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Revenue mix by service
segments.commentary: Surgical services 66% of group revenue; diagnosis consultations and non-surgical 12%; optical and pharmacy 22%.

segments.name: Vintage cohorts
segments.commentary: Pre-FY23 facilities INR 948 crores (75% of revenue), up 17.2%; FY24 cohort INR 96 crores, up 20.9%; FY25 cohort INR 127 crores, up 67.8% (includes Thind acquisition, about INR 42 crores in H1); FY26 cohort INR 71 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 facility additions raised to 65 (from 60), including 55 surgical centres (from 40) and 10 primary centres.
H1 FY27 delivered 39 additions (34 surgical); H2 plan is 26 facilities (21 surgical). Regional split for FY27: South 25, North 20, West 15, East 5.
Capex guidance raised to INR 500 crores from INR 400 crores earlier.
Management expects Delhi NCR to add 8-12 more centres over the next 9-12 months.
High-end cataract mix expected to stabilise around 30-35% of cataract surgeries for the next few years, not 50-60%.
capex_capacity: Network: 305 facilities in India across 14 states and 5 UTs (172 cities); total network 324 including 6% international. Tier 1 share 32%, other markets 62%.
H1 FY27 volume: about 18.5 lakh patients, over 1.86 lakh surgeries (+19% YoY), about 1,250 surgeries per day.
Average surgical centre generates INR 75-80 lakh revenue per month; several centres reached breakeven in core markets.
Lenticular (SMILE) machines added at Naranpura, Cochin and Coimbatore; femto cataract procedures 3,284 in H1 (+25.5%).
Pinhole pupilloplasty (PPP) department launched at Chennai flagship; over 540 PPP surgeries in H1 vs 500 in full FY26.
demand_pricing: H1 SSSG growth split: OPD/volume growth about 7.5%, conversion about 0.5%, value growth about 9.5% (premiumisation about 8%, price about 1.5%).
Cataract and refractive surgery volumes grew about 20% YoY in H1; cataract about 73% of surgeries, refractive about 4.7%.
Lenticular procedures +41.9% YoY in H1 as market shifts from LASIK to SMILE; yield improvement attributed to mix shift.
H1 payer mix: 63% cash, 28% insurance and TPA, 9% government schemes. India revenue H1 INR 1,138 crores (+28.5%): volume +8%, value +9.5%, balance from new centres.
Management says the market is not yet seeing a shift in the core high-end mix beyond about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale and financial profile of the acquisition; how acquisitions fit expansion strategy.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired two Delhi NCR centres (Greater Kailash and Loni, Ghaziabad) from Dr. Anchal Gupta for about INR 55 crores; trailing revenue about INR 13.5 crores and business EBITDA about INR 7.16 crores. About INR 33 crores paid upfront, balance over 4 years on milestones. Acquisitions limited to new markets at the right multiple; none planned in Chennai, Bengaluru or Hyderabad.

qa_highlights.question: Revised capex and facility guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Capex raised to INR 500 crores from INR 400 crores; 65 facilities for FY27 including 55 surgical centres. Management said planning pipeline is about 100 sites for about 60 centres per year, set 12-18 months ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Split of SSSG growth into footfall, conversion and realisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Volume about 8% (OPD about 7.5%, conversion 0.5%); value about 9.5%, of which premiumisation about 8% and price about 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Losses from new facilities and related cost lines.
qa_highlights.answer: Losses about INR 42 crores in H1 across FY26 and FY27 cohorts (FY27 cohort INR 18.2 crores; FY26 cohort INR 20.12 crores). Consultancy charges about INR 96 crores; depreciation base INR 80-83 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Doctor attrition and fellowship retention.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall attrition about 14-15% including trainees, senior attrition 1-2%, similar across regions; exact figures and fellowship retention to be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Sun Pharma eye-drop production halt on pharmacy business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact; Sun Pharma is not a significant part of the pharmaceutical supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: Regulatory risk on drug, device and implant markup caps.
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it premature to comment while Supreme Court and government discussions are ongoing.

risks_watch: Start-up losses at 51 recently launched surgical facilities (about INR 42 crores in H1), with the FY27 cohort at INR 18.2 crores.
Pace of H2 rollout (26 facilities) and ramp-up of newer centres; execution risk on raised guidance.
Possible regulatory intervention on hospital drug, device and implant markups, which could hit margins including IOL pricing; management declined to size it.
Rising competition in Delhi NCR and South Delhi, where the acquisition was used to gain presence.
Doctor attrition about 14-15% overall; exact data still pending.
Pending delisting/merger steps: subsidiary trading stops November 17, with share allocation from November 18 onwards.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, volumes and guidance upgrades. Management was openly evasive or deferred on doctor attrition, fellowship retention and regulatory markup risk, promising follow-ups.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 FY27 was another quarter of strong and consistent performance.
We are now targeting an addition of 65 new facilities during the year, which includes 55 new surgical facilities as against the earlier guidance of 60 facilities, which included 40 surgical centers.
We will be revising our capex guidance upwards from INR 400 crores to INR 500 crores.
The growth engine for the company continues to remain organic expansion.

adds.what: Facility additions FY27 total 65 (55 surgical, 10 primary); H1 delivered 39, H2 plan 26 (21 surgical)
Delhi NCR to add 8-12 more centres over next 9-12 months

growth.why: Management raised FY27 facility additions to 65 (55 surgical) and capex to INR 500 crore, with H1 already delivering 39 additions and a specific H2 plan of 26 facilities by region; H1 revenue growth of 28.7% and SSSG of 17.7% support the outlook, though the revenue growth figure is an H1 actual rather than a formal full-year guide.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ind AS EBITDA margin held near 28% and PAT margin rose about 134 bps to 8.5% in Q2, though start-up losses of about INR 42 crores in H1 from 51 newer centres cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: H1 already delivered 39 additions (34 surgical) and the H2 plan of 26 facilities (21 surgical) is under construction, with FY27 capex raised to INR 500 crores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 surgeries rose 19% YoY to over 1.86 lakh, SSSG was 17.7% in H1 with OPD/volume growth about 7.5%, and 26 more facilities are planned in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was raised to INR 500 crores from INR 400 crores, the planning pipeline is about 100 sites for about 60 centres a year, and Delhi NCR is to add 8-12 centres over 9-12 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was already raised to 65 additions (from 60) and H1 revenue grew 28.7% YoY, so a further upgrade depends on H2 rollout delivery against the 26-facility plan.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on the 26-facility H2 rollout and start-up losses (FY27 cohort INR 18.2 crores in H1) could slow ramp-up, and the regulatory markup cap is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pinhole pupilloplasty was launched at Chennai flagship (over 540 PPP surgeries in H1) and SMILE machines were added at three centres, but no further launch dates were given.

rows.label: Drug, device and implant markup caps
rows.why: Management declined to size the risk while Supreme Court and government talks are ongoing, and it could hit margins including IOL pricing.

rows.label: Delhi NCR expansion after acquisition
rows.why: Delhi NCR network is 15 facilities after 5 Greenfield and 2 acquired centres, with 8-12 more planned over 9-12 months and acquisitions limited to new markets at the right multiple.

rows.label: Delisting/merger share allocation
rows.why: Subsidiary trading stops 17 November with share allocation starting 18 November, as already scheduled in the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on facility additions, volumes, SSSG and the capex upgrade, but deferred on doctor attrition, fellowship retention and markup-cap regulation; the call touched on start-up losses and execution risk for the H2 rollout.
